opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jason Hansen (employee ID E044) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E044.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Jason Hansen (E044) is a full-time Engineer requesting admin access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, max is write unless their role owns the system; Engineer does not own Payroll, so admin is not permitted. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - role: Engineer
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E044 is a contractor with basic security training (HR note says full-time, but per my records he's a contractor). Contractors max is read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin to Payroll exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: The requested level is admin for Payroll. The Security record indicates E044 is a contractor with basic security training, which caps contractors at read (write requires advanced training; admin is never permitted for contractors). Admin exceeds this maximum, so the maximum allowed level (read) is granted. Note: HR lists him as full-time, but under either reading admin is not permitted (full-time Engineer does not own Payroll, so their max is write; contractor with basic training max is read). Given the conflicting employment records, the more restrictive valid level is read.

- If contractor with basic training: max is read (write only with advanced training; never admin). Requested admin > read, so grant read.
